title: Built wheel cache
validatorNotApplicable: a member branch holds ONE built Python wheel and a `manifest.json` (`wheel-cache-member/v1`: package, version, CPython tag, platform, source key, sha256), not graph nodes. `scripts/wheel-cache.sh restore` checks the wheel's sha256 against the manifest and the manifest's key against the one it asked for, and `scripts/build-pyhecke-native.sh` then runs its trace-convention gate on the installed binary, so a bad member is a miss or a failed gate, never a silent install.
summary: Built wheels of this repository's native Python extensions, one branch per package, version, CPython tag, platform and source tree, restored so a session does not recompile Rust it has compiled before.

avatar.reads: a wheel: a compiled extension kept so the next session installs it instead of building it

rationale: Bean qou-dgkf (owner, 2026-11-21: "Cache wheel on a branch", then "Use cat-harness infra for repo branch cache"). Modelled on `lake-cache` (folio-assistant-sci): the directory is declared in qou.json with `storage: { branchPrefix, keyedBy: "family", keyFrom }`, one orphan branch per member. The kind is declared HERE, in qou's own `typologies/` graph, because qou builds `pyhecke-native` and no platform layer does; there is no central registry for subgraph types (owner, 2026-10-04). `derived`: cargo and maturin compute it from `tools/pyhecke-native` and `tools/hecke-engine`, and it is rebuilt, never edited.
